mtmayon.name: Mount Mayon
mtmayon.summary: Active stratovolcano on the **Bicol Volcanic Arc**, and the most active volcano in the Philippines with 52+ eruptions in 500 years.[^1] It is among the most symmetrical volcanic cones on Earth — the "perfect cone" that rises 2,421 m from Albay Gulf.[^2] The VEI 4 eruption of 1814 buried the town of Cagsawa and killed roughly 1,200 people; only the church bell tower survived.[^1] It was the Philippines' first national park (1938), and its caldera is the core of the UNESCO Albay Biosphere Reserve.[^2] In pre-colonial Bicolano tradition it is the abode of **Daragang Magayon** and the supreme god Gugurang.[^1] Activity continues: PHIVOLCS raised the alert level to 3 after a magmatic eruption on 6 January 2026.[^3]

mtkanlaon.name: Mount Kanlaon
mtkanlaon.summary: Active andesitic stratovolcano on the **Negros Volcanic Belt**, and the highest peak in the Visayas at 2,465 m — also the highest mountain on Negros Island and the 42nd-highest island peak on Earth.[^4] It has erupted more than 40 times since 1819 and is the most active volcano in the Visayas; eruptions are usually phreatic, throwing ash and steam from the summit Lugud crater.[^5] The name means "place of Laon", after the pre-colonial Visayan goddess of creation and agriculture.[^6] Its southwestern flank carries the **La Castellana debris avalanche** — at 13 km³ over a 33 km run-out, the largest known debris flow in the Philippines.[^5] A 2024–2026 unrest sequence has produced a VEI 3 eruption, 87,000 evacuated, and further moderately explosive eruptions through 2026.[^7]

mtisarog.name: Mount Isarog
mtisarog.summary: Active stratovolcano on the Bicol Volcanic Arc, 2,000 m high with a 2,500 m-wide summit crater breached east and drained by the Rangas River.[^8] A Holocene sector collapse of its northwestern flank sent the **Tinambac debris avalanche** all the way into San Miguel Bay.[^8] Its last eruption was in the 12th century CE — a potsherd found under the ash proves people already lived at Goa at the time.[^9] It shows gas seepages, warm springs and steaming vents today.[^8] The summit is the meeting point of six municipalities and Naga City.[^8] It is an ultra-prominent peak, and home to endemic species including the Isarog shrew rat, the Isarog cloud frog and the Isarog forest skink.[^10]

mtbuddajo.name: Mount Bud Dajo
mtbuddajo.summary: A 620 m **cinder cone** on Jolo island, part of the Zamboanga–Sulu volcanic arc, and the second-highest point in Sulu.[^11] The summit crater is 0.5 km across and breached to the southwest, and the cone's base spans 9.5 km.[^12] The volcano is extinct — its last eruption date is unknown, and PHIVOLCS monitoring surveys in 1993 and 1997 found nothing unusual.[^11] It has been a sacred mountain to the Tausug people since before Spanish contact, and became Mount Dajo National Park in 1938.[^11] It is also remembered as the site of the 1906 First Battle of Bud Dajo.[^13]

mtpinatubo.name: Mount Pinatubo
mtpinatubo.summary: Active stratovolcano in the Zambales Mountains, now 1,486 m — it stood at 1,745 m before 15 June 1991, when it produced a **VEI 6 eruption**, the second-largest terrestrial eruption of the 20th century.[^14] It ejected about 10 km³ of magma and a 35 km ash column, put more particulate into the stratosphere than any eruption since Krakatoa, and cooled global temperatures by roughly 0.5 °C across 1991–1993.[^14] It happened to coincide with Typhoon Yunya, whose rain and wind drove the ash into communities already buried by pyroclastic flows.[^15] The 2.5 km caldera now holds Lake Pinatubo, drained by hand in 2001 after fears of a wall collapse.[^16] The Aeta people of the surrounding slopes hold ancestral domain titles over parts of the mountain.[^17] Last eruption: a weak phreatic explosion on 30 November 2021.[^18]

mttaal.name: Mount Taal
mttaal.short: Volcano island in a caldera lake
mttaal.summary: A 25–30 km flooded caldera, the second most active volcano in the Philippines with 39 confirmed historical eruptions, and one of the Smithsonian's "Decade Volcanoes" for its deadly proximity to populated land.[^19] Volcano Island sits in the middle of Taal Lake, and its 2 km Main Crater holds a lake with Vulcan Point, a small rocky islet that was one of the largest third-order islands in the world.[^20] The 1754 VEI 5 eruption was its largest; the 1911 eruption killed about 1,100 people, obliterated the crater floor and created the crater lake.[^21] The overall recorded death toll is around 6,000.[^19] Volcano Island is permanently off-limits — a Permanent Danger Zone.[^22] Last eruption: 8 October 2026.[^23]

mtbanahaw.name: Mount Banahaw
mtbanahaw.summary: A three-peaked **active complex volcano** on the Luzon Volcanic Arc, 2,170 m — the highest mountain in Laguna, in Quezon, and in the whole CALABARZON region.[^24] Its summit holds a 1.5 × 3.5 km, 210 m-deep caldera, breached on the southern rim by the 1730 eruption; a lake occupied the crater before that, and the resulting mudflow destroyed the town of Sariaya below the mountain.[^25] It is a sacred mountain and a long-standing pilgrimage destination, and its springs are drawn from for "holy water".[^25] The surrounding Makiling–Banahaw Watershed supplies steam for power generation.[^26] Most of it lies in the Mounts Banahaw–San Cristobal Protected Landscape (10,901 ha); climbing has been suspended since 2004, with some sections reopened in 2019.[^27] Four endemic rodents live here, including the Banahaw tree mouse.[^28]

mthibokhibok.name: Mount Hibok-Hibok
mthibokhibok.summary: An active stratovolcano on **Camiguin island** — the Philippines' only volcanic island — 1,332 m high with a 10 km base, also known as Catarman Volcano.[^29] It has erupted four times in modern history. The 1871 flank eruption built the cone of Mount Vulcan, the youngest volcano on the island.[^30] The 1948–51 sequence was the deadly one: the 1951 eruption on 4 December killed over 3,000 people, and Camiguin's population fell from 69,000 to about 34,000 through emigration.[^31] It has six hot springs and three craters, and the nearby White Island is a popular dive.[^29] Together with Mount Timpoong it forms a natural monument that became an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2015.[^32]

lakebuhi.name: Lake Buhi
lakebuhi.summary: Not a volcano but a volcanic accident: a **1,707 ha lake** (17.07 km², 8 m average depth, 120 m surface elevation) formed in 1641 when an earthquake caused one flank of Mount Iriga — also called Mount Asog — to collapse, the landslide creating a natural dam across the local streams.[^33] It is famous for the **sinarapan** (*Mistichthys luzonensis*), the world's smallest commercially harvested fish.[^34] The lake also feeds the National Power Corporation's hydro plant (about 2.8 MW) and irrigates at least 100 km² of the Riconada towns downstream.[^35] The surrounding forest holds five endemic bird species.[^34]
